rust_doctor_covered: All 18 rust-doctor diagnostics are represented in the 12 rust-doctor-tagged findings; GC-002 batches the 7 channel.rs indexing_slicing findings (lines 128, 134, 149, 152, 161, 164, 167) into a single entry with full line list.

findings.title: parse_start_command cyclomatic 15 / cognitive 26
findings.description: parse_start_command combines argument tokenization, per-flag branching (--preset, --role, --topic, default), flag-eating defense, and final validation in one ~70-line body. The three flag branches each have a (advance-i, bounds-check, anti-flag-eating-check) preamble that is copy-pasted.
findings.trigger: Future flag additions (--model, --provider, etc.) will multiply the copy-pasted preamble; readers must hold the whole loop in their head to verify the bounds-check order.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a helper `fn take_value<'a>(tokens: &[String], i: &mut usize) -> Option<&'a str>` that does the bounds-check + anti-flag-eating check, returning None on either failure. Replace each branch's preamble with `let v = take_value(&tokens, &mut i)?;`. Drops CC significantly without changing behavior.

findings.title: channel.rs indexing_slicing (7 occurrences on already-bounds-checked indices)
findings.description: Inside parse_start_command, every `tokens[i]` access is preceded by an explicit `if i >= tokens.len() { return None; }` guard. The panicking index is therefore unreachable, but clippy::indexing_slicing (pedantic, enabled via `-D warnings`) still fires and the project uses `-D warnings`. Lines: 128, 134, 149, 152, 161, 164, 167.
findings.trigger: Build fails under `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`. False positives that the project's lint policy does not allow to be silenced ad-hoc.

findings.title: tokenize cyclomatic 14 / cognitive 38 — quote-state machine intermixed with whitespace handling
findings.description: tokenize's loop has 7 match arms each pushing to one of two accumulators (current, quoted) and managing the escape / unclosed-quote fallback inline. The nested escape branch (lines 244-258) handles '\' before the matching quote char by re-emitting the backslash, which is not standard shell behavior and is undocumented.
findings.trigger: Future changes to escape handling (e.g., adding \n, \t) require touching 4 nested branches; the unclosed-quote fallback (`quoted.insert(0, quote)`) is also non-obvious.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract `fn read_quoted(chars: &mut Peekable<...>, quote: char) -> String` that owns the inside-of-quotes state machine, returning the literal content (with unclosed-quote prefix appended by the caller). Pull the escape policy into a single 5-line match on `escaped`.

findings.title: coordinator.rs test_parse_coordinator_plan_with_markdown_wrapper duplicates test_parse_coordinator_plan_valid
findings.description: Two unit tests share the parse-then-assert-skeleton structure (only the input string and one literal differ). The cross-file match (tools/markdown_skill/parser.rs) is a separate test pattern that incidentally shares structure.
findings.trigger: Adding a new field to RespondentPlan forces both tests to be updated in lockstep, with no guarantee both stay consistent.
findings.suggested_fix:
Collapse into a single parameterized test:
```
#[test_case(r#"{"respondents":[{"persona_id":"arch",...}],"need_summary":true}"#, true; "plain json")]
#[test_case("```json\n{...}\n```", false; "markdown fence")]
fn parses(input: &str, expect_summary: bool) { ... }
```
or accept the duplication as test boilerplate and ignore the lint on this file (test code is allowed to repeat itself for clarity).

findings.title: executor.rs is 1186 lines — split before growth makes the split harder
findings.description: A single file holds: provider resolution, persistence, the coordinator round driver (execute_round, 356 lines), 6 mock LLM test fixtures, and 11 round-driving tests. Concerns are mixed.
findings.trigger: Adding streaming / tool-call / multi-round retry will balloon the file further.
findings.suggested_fix:
Split into:
- `executor/mod.rs` (struct + execute_round skeleton)
- `executor/provider_resolver.rs` (resolve_provider + provider_fallback_warned)
- `executor/persist.rs` (persist_turn + DB error handling)
- `executor/round.rs` (execute_round body — or break into pre_prompt/coordinator/personas/commit phases)
- `executor/tests.rs` (current `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`)

This is a large refactor; defer until next LLM-loop change.

findings.title: execute_round spans 356 lines — single function holds four phases
findings.description: execute_round interleaves (a) round-budget gate, (b) coordinator LLM call + cancel select, (c) plan parsing + dropped-target detection, (d) per-persona LLM loop with prior-discussion accumulation, (e) commit phase (history mutation + DB persist + message build). The 200-line mid-block (steps c–d) is the densest region.
findings.trigger: Adding a feature (e.g., retry on persona 503) requires touching both the LLM-loop body and the commit-phase rollback path; current shape makes the rollback contract hard to see.
findings.suggested_fix:
Extract helpers:
- `async fn call_coordinator(&self, prompt, cancel) -> Result<String, GroupChatError>`
- `fn detect_dropped_targets(targets, participants, plan) -> Vec<String>`
- `async fn call_personas(&self, plan, participants, ...) -> Result<Vec<PreparedResponse>, GroupChatError>`
- `fn commit_round(session, round, prepared, dropped_targets) -> Vec<GroupChatMessage>` (synchronous; no DB call)
- `async fn persist_round(self, session_id, staged_turns)` (best-effort)

execute_round becomes ~30 lines orchestrating the five.

findings.title: executor.rs:456 staging_turns[0] indexing
findings.description: `staged_turns[0].3.clone()` is preceded by `if prepared.is_empty() { return Ok(messages); }`, so the index is in-bounds. The author added a safety comment. clippy::indexing_slicing still fires under `-D warnings`.
findings.trigger: Build fails under `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`. Comment is good documentation but does not satisfy the linter.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind the user turn at the top of execute_round into a `let user_turn_text = user_message.to_string();` and clone that instead. The staged_turns Vec still holds the same String by value; cloning the local binding avoids the index.

findings.title: executor.rs tests module is 656 lines
findings.description: The test module contains 11 round-driving tests and 6 mock-provider fixtures (SequentialMockProvider, FailingProvider, CoordinatorOnlyProvider, EchoAfterCoordinator, TwoCallProvider, PartialFailProvider). Test code is acceptable to be large but 656 lines is at the boundary of unreadable.
findings.trigger: Future tests will keep appending; the file is approaching the 1k-line ceiling where grep becomes the only navigation.
findings.suggested_fix: Move mock providers to `tests/common/mod.rs` and round-driving tests stay in the file. Tests do not need to live in the same binary as production code; a `tests/executor.rs` integration test file would isolate them.

findings.title: executor.rs tests — 6 near-duplicate mock-provider implementations
findings.description: Each test fixture defines its own mock struct that implements `AiProvider::process` by branching on a call counter. The implementations differ only in the response sequence / failure mode. Spans: 615–660, 662–686, 810–835, 837–868, 930–961, 1012–1041 (rust-doctor similarity 80.7%).
findings.trigger: Adding a new test fixture (e.g., for streaming responses) requires copy-pasting the boilerplate; bugs in the mock pattern propagate to every fixture.

findings.title: orchestrator.rs tests — 3 near-duplicate session-creation tests
findings.description: Three tests (test_create_session, test_create_session_preset_not_found, test_create_session_too_many_personas) follow the same skeleton: build sources → call create_session → assert is_ok / unwrap_err / pattern-match. Lines 402–421, 448–469, 575–607 (similarity 82.7%).
findings.trigger: Adding a new validation error path (e.g., InvalidPersona) requires copy-pasting the skeleton.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `#[test_case(...)]` parameterized tests, or accept the duplication as table-driven test clarity. Lower priority than executor fixture dedup since these are short (≤30 lines each).

findings.title: orchestrator.rs tests — 2 near-duplicate session-creation tests
findings.description: test_create_session_invalid_inline_persona and test_create_session_rejects_duplicate_persona_ids are 65-node duplicates (lines 448–469, 545–573). Both build an inline persona + a preset, call create_session, and assert InvalidPersona.
findings.trigger: Same as GC-010 — adding validation cases needs duplicate skeleton work.
findings.suggested_fix: Consolidate into a single test that calls create_session with two invalid setups, or extract a helper `fn assert_invalid_inline(orch, sources, expected_msg_contains)`.

findings.title: session.rs tests — 3 near-duplicate add_turn tests
findings.description: test_add_turn, test_build_history_text, test_add_turn_rejects_non_monotonic_round all follow: make_session → add_turn (1..3x) → assert history.len/current_round. Similarity 81.3%.
findings.trigger: Future regression tests for add_turn (e.g., timestamp preservation, speaker ordering) require copy-pasting the skeleton.
findings.suggested_fix: Extract a `fn make_session_with_history(round_seq: &[(u32, Speaker, &str)]) -> GroupChatSession` helper. Each test asserts a single property against the pre-loaded session.

findings.title: Silent std::sync::Mutex poisoning recovery across 5 sites in orchestrator.rs
findings.description: `self.sessions.lock().unwrap_or_else(|e| e.into_inner())` recovers silently from a poisoned mutex. A thread panic while holding the sessions-map guard means subsequent inserts/gets/removes/all_sessions operate on a HashMap that may have been mutated mid-operation by the panicking thread. The recovery pattern is repeated at: create_session (line 182), get_session (226), remove_session (298), all_sessions (324), and inside execute_round resolve_provider at executor.rs:116 (provider_fallback_warned mutex).
findings.trigger: If any panicking path is added that holds the orchestrator lock — e.g., a future caller that catches an error and tries to log+continue while the map is being mutated — the silent recovery hides a use-after-panic bug. Worse, the in-memory sessions map could contain entries from before the panic AND after, with no transactional boundary.

findings.title: Silent std::sync::Mutex poisoning recovery on executor.rs provider_fallback_warned
findings.description: Same pattern as GC-013 on a different mutex. Three sites (resolve_provider production:116, test_resolve_provider_warn_is_deduped x2: 1170, 1179) silently recover from poisoning on a HashSet<(String,String)>. The HashSet itself is harder to corrupt than a HashMap but the pattern is the same — a panic during the critical section silently continues.
findings.trigger: Future code that panics inside the insert (e.g., a tracing! macro that panics, a Clone impl that panics on a corrupted String) would be silently absorbed.
findings.suggested_fix: Same as GC-013 — log on poisoning, then recover. Or use `parking_lot::Mutex` (this project uses `crate::sync_primitives::Mutex`, so check whether that alias supports non-poisoning semantics).

findings.title: tokio::select! on provider.process() may not be cancel-safe depending on provider impl
findings.description: Two tokio::select! sites (lines 253 coordinator call, 399 persona call) race `provider.process(RequestPayload)` against `cancel.cancelled()`. Cancellation drops the provider future mid-flight. If the provider implementation streams partial response bytes (e.g., a SSE-based Anthropic adapter), dropping the future can: leave the underlying HTTP body in an indeterminate state; leak the reqwest::Response (held by the future); lose partial work the provider had already accounted toward billing.
findings.trigger: An end_session fired mid-round drops both the coordinator future (if in flight) and any in-flight persona future. For HTTP/1.1 chunked providers, the connection is closed cleanly; for SSE-based providers with bidirectional state (tool-call acknowledgements), this could leak server-side state until the provider's own timeout fires.
findings.suggested_fix:
Audit each `AiProvider::process` impl in `src/providers/` for cancellation safety. If any are not cancel-safe, switch the cancel branch to use `provider.process(...).take_until(cancel.cancelled())` which guarantees the future is awaited to completion, OR introduce a provider-level "abort" that flushes state before returning.

Lower-priority mitigation: wrap each provider call in a `tokio::time::timeout` whose drop guarantees reqwest::Response cleanup.

findings.title: execute_round commits session.history BEFORE DB persist completes (acknowledged asymmetry)
findings.description: Lines 449–470 mutate session.history and session.current_round, then lines 472–480 best-effort persist to DB. If the process is killed (panic, SIGKILL, OOM) between history commit and DB persist completion, the in-memory session is one round ahead of the persisted table. On the next round, the in-memory add_turn is gated by `if round < current_round` (session.rs:147), which is fine for monotonic rounds, but the persisted `group_chat_turns` table has a permanent gap that replays will surface.
findings.trigger: Process crash mid-commit. Recoverable on the next round if the user re-sends the message; otherwise the session is silently out of sync between memory and DB until end_session runs.
findings.suggested_fix:
Already documented in the executor.rs comment as a known asymmetry. Two minimal fixes:
(a) Persist FIRST, then mutate history — but DB failure is best-effort so this would mean DB-first success but history inconsistency on failure. Worse trade-off.
(b) Wrap the persist loop in `tokio::time::timeout` and warn-on-failure; the comment already says this is recoverable on the next round. The current order (memory-first) is the correct trade-off; flag this for a future transactionally-bounded store.

Acceptable as-is, but the comment could call out the recovery path explicitly so on-call engineers know the in-memory state is authoritative during recovery.

findings.title: session.rs add_turn is pub but only called from executor — leaks internal API
findings.description: `pub fn add_turn(&mut self, ...)` is publicly exported via mod.rs `pub use session::GroupChatSession`. Any external caller (channels, harness, future code) can call add_turn directly and bypass the Active-status check by checking it themselves — defeating the gate that protects against out-of-order turns (session.rs:144-152).
findings.trigger: A future channel implementation that writes turns directly into the session (bypassing execute_round) would re-introduce the same bug that the add_turn test_add_turn_rejects_non_monotonic_round test was written to prevent.
findings.current_code: pub fn add_turn(&mut self, round: u32, speaker: Speaker, content: String) { ... }
findings.suggested_fix: Change to `pub(crate) fn add_turn(...)` if module-only access is intended. Note: GroupChatSession is `pub use`d, so pub(crate) inside the module keeps it inaccessible from outside `crate::group_chat`. Verify no external caller exists by grepping for `GroupChatSession` outside the module.

findings.title: GroupChatOrchestrator::create_session / end_session take &mut self unnecessarily
findings.description: create_session (line 86) and end_session (line 269) take `&mut self` but every field they touch (`sessions: Mutex<HashMap<...>>`, `persona_registry: PersonaRegistry` with `&self` resolve, `config: GroupChatConfig` with `&self` read) is internally mutable via Mutex or read-only. The &mut self requirement forces callers to hold an exclusive borrow, preventing concurrent create_session calls on the same orchestrator from different tasks.
findings.trigger: The dispatch layer (group_chat command handler) needs to call create_session while another handler is calling get_session — the &mut self requirement serializes them. Today this is OK because the dispatch layer holds the orchestrator behind a Mutex too, but the double-locking is brittle.
findings.suggested_fix:
Change to `&self`. Mutex internally serializes the map mutation, and `persona_registry.resolve` already takes `&self`. Verify no test relies on &mut self for compile-time mutation tracking (a quick grep should suffice).

This is API-friction only; runtime behavior is identical.

findings.title: O(n) lookup of persona by id inside execute_round persona loop
findings.description: For each respondent, execute_round does `session.participants.iter().find(|p| p.id == respondent.persona_id)` — O(n) per respondent, total O(n*m) per round. For typical session sizes (2–4 personas) this is irrelevant; flagged only because the orchestrator already validates persona IDs (orchestrator.rs step 3a) and could pass a `HashMap<&str, &Persona>` index to skip the lookup.
findings.trigger: Sessions approaching the configured max_personas_per_session ceiling with full coordinator plans.

findings.title: executor.rs provider_fallback_warned HashSet grows without explicit bound
findings.description: The dedupe set is keyed on `(persona_id, provider_name)` pairs and grows monotonically — entries are only ever inserted, never removed. Bounded in practice by the number of distinct (persona, provider_name) combinations in the configuration, but in a long-running server with dynamically added personas (e.g., per-request inline personas with provider overrides) the set grows per session.
findings.trigger: Long-running orchestrator with many inline personas referencing many provider names.
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) cap the set with an LRU (e.g., `lru::LruCache` with capacity 256), or (b) document the upper bound (number of distinct persona_id × provider_name pairs) and accept it. Inline personas typically don't have provider overrides (default None), so the practical bound is small.

findings.title: coordinator.rs truncate_str is a 1-line wrapper around crate::utils::text_format::truncate_chars
findings.description: Local `fn truncate_str(s: &str, max_len: usize) -> &str { crate::utils::text_format::truncate_chars(s, max_len) }` adds no behavior and exists only to shorten call sites (3 uses in this file).
findings.trigger: Reader confusion: a new maintainer sees truncate_str and wonders if it differs from the canonical helper.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `crate::utils::text_format::truncate_chars` directly, or import it as `use crate::utils::text_format::truncate_chars;` and rename locally. The wrapper is a missed opportunity for an alias.

findings.title: build_history_text / build_history_text_windowed use let _ = writeln! to discard infallible Result
findings.description: `let _ = writeln!(text, ...)` discards the Result. For `String`, `fmt::Write::write_str` is infallible (returns Ok(()) always) so the discard is safe, but clippy::let_underscore_must_use (if enabled) or pedantic lints may flag this.
findings.trigger: Cosmetic lint noise; no functional risk because `String` writes cannot fail.
findings.suggested_fix:
Use `.unwrap()` since it's infallible:
```
writeln!(text, "[{}]: {}\n", turn.speaker.name(), turn.content).unwrap();
```
or use the format! idiom with push_str to avoid the macro altogether. Both are stylistic; the current code is correct.

findings.title: build_coordinator_prompt inner fn quote_field is a nested function
findings.description: `fn quote_field(s: &str) -> String { s.replace('"', "\u{201D}") }` is defined inside `build_coordinator_prompt` (a free function). Nested functions in Rust are uncommon and the helper has clear module-level reusability.
findings.trigger: Future use of the same quote-replacement in build_persona_prompt would force another nested fn or an inline copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Move `quote_field` to the helpers section alongside `truncate_str` and `strip_markdown_fences`. Module-private fn, single definition, two callers (build_coordinator_prompt, build_persona_prompt — the latter also replaces '"' with '\u{201D}' inline at line 137–138, which is itself a missed reuse opportunity).
